criteria.text: Diagnosis of persistent or recurring Cushing's disease (approval criterion 3).
Patient is 18 years of age or older (approval criterion 1).
Prescribed by or in consultation with a physician specializing in the patient's diagnosis, or in consultation with an endocrinologist (approval criterion 2).

Pituitary surgery is not an option, or pituitary surgery or repeat surgeries, with or without radiation therapy, have not been curative; patient still requires a cortisol synthesis inhibitor (approval criterion 3).

Documented failure, contraindication, or intolerance to TWO of oral ketoconazole, oral cabergoline, oral Metopirone (metyrapone), or oral Lysodren (mitotane), for at least 30 days each (approval criterion 4).
Urine free cortisol levels obtained; normal ranges stated in source: <150 nmol/24 hours OR 3.5–45 mcg/24 hours. Normalization is not an initial approval requirement (first approval criterion 5).
Baseline ECG obtained and will be monitored periodically (second approval criterion 5).
Baseline serum potassium and magnesium obtained and corrected if abnormal before starting therapy; will monitor periodically during treatment (source approval criterion 6).
Patient is not currently lactating (denial criterion 2: female and currently lactating).
Patient has no symptoms of adrenal insufficiency (denial criterion 3).

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Isturisa (osilodrostat) Criteria Version 1. Original: 7/6/2021; Approval: 9/17/21; Effective: 11/1/21.

Encoded: all seven approval requirements and denial criteria 2–3. Source approval numbering repeats 5 for ECG and ends at 6 for electrolytes. Failure to meet approval criteria is also a denial. Surgery eligibility, prior therapy, laboratory testing and monitoring commitments are attestations requiring documentation verification.

Cautions (notes only): monitor closely for hypocortisolism and potentially life-threatening adrenal insufficiency; dosage reduction or interruption may be necessary. Dosages may need adjustment for hepatic impairment. Use caution with risk factors for QTc prolongation. Monitor for hypokalemia, worsening hypertension, edema, and hirsutism.

Duration (notes only): initial approval up to 3 months; reauthorization up to 6 months if prescriber documents achievement and maintenance of THREE of five response criteria: urinary free cortisol (UFC) at or below the upper limit of normal (ULN); cortisol levels within normal limits; no symptoms consistent with Cushing's disease; no evidence or symptoms of hypocortisolism; no evidence of disease progression.
Quantity (notes only): 30-day supply, not to exceed 60 mg/day. Numeric quantity enforcement is not encoded.
Documentation verification, cautions, ongoing monitoring, duration, reauthorization and quantity limits require manual review; this pack remains partial.
